morphology.shape: C-shaped trypomastigote in blood; intracellular amastigote in tissue

protozoanDetails.lifeCycleForm: Trypomastigote (bloodstream, infective/diagnostic form) and amastigote (intracellular tissue form, e.g. in cardiac/smooth muscle)

habitat.naturalHabitat: Blood and tissues (especially cardiac and smooth muscle) of mammalian hosts; gut of triatomine ("kissing") bugs
habitat.hostAssociation: Zoonotic — many wild and domestic mammals serve as reservoirs
habitat.environmentalOccurrence: Endemic to rural areas of Latin America where triatomine bugs inhabit poor-quality housing
habitat.reservoir: Wild and domestic mammals; triatomine bug vector

microscopy.appearance: C- or S-shaped trypomastigotes with a large kinetoplast near the posterior end, undulating membrane, and single flagellum
microscopy.arrangement: Free trypomastigotes in blood during acute infection

culture.media: Specialized media (e.g. NNN medium) in reference laboratories
culture.growthCharacteristics: Fastidious; culture mainly used in reference/research settings

identificationClues: Trypomastigotes visible on blood smear during the acute phase only
Serology is the primary diagnostic method in chronic infection, when parasitemia is very low
Romaña's sign — periorbital swelling at the site of vector inoculation near the eye
Chagoma — localized skin swelling at the bite site

diseases: Chagas disease (American trypanosomiasis) — acute phase, followed by an often asymptomatic indeterminate phase
clinicalImportance.transmission: Contact with feces of an infected triatomine ("kissing") bug, typically through a bite wound or mucous membranes; also congenital, blood transfusion, and organ transplantation
clinicalImportance.epidemiology: Endemic to Latin America, particularly in areas with substandard rural housing that harbors triatomine bugs; a leading cause of infectious cardiomyopathy in endemic regions
clinicalImportance.labSignificance: Diagnosis shifts from direct parasite visualization in the acute phase to serologic testing in the chronic phase due to declining parasitemia

examFacts.keyBiochemicalReaction: Not applicable — blood smear (acute) or serology (chronic)
examFacts.importantTest: Giemsa blood smear (acute phase); serology (chronic phase)
examFacts.distinguishingFeature: Transmitted through triatomine bug feces (contamination of the bite wound), not through the bite itself
